name: Dimeticone (head lice)
className: Physically acting head lice treatment (silicone; non-insecticidal)

formulations.label: Head lice shampoo
formulations.strengths: Dimeticone (clinic product; strength not given). UK product used: dimeticone 4% w/w cutaneous solution
formulations.note: No UK SmPC for a dimeticone head lice shampoo was found. The UK SmPCs are for a dimeticone 4% w/w cutaneous solution (lotion) left on dry hair for at least 8 hours. The information below comes from those SmPCs; follow the clinic product's own directions for use.

src.q: Dimeticone 4% w/w
3. Pharmaceutical form Cutaneous solution

bnf.note: BNF/BNFC is only available in the UK; not accessed.

items.t: Eradication of head lice infestation.

src.q: Hedrin is indicated for the eradication of headlice infestations

restrictions.note: The UK dimeticone 4% SmPCs state no prescribing restrictions. No NICE guidance on head lice was found (CKS is geo-blocked and not used).

items.t: Apply enough lotion to cover dry hair from roots to tips so no part of the scalp is missed. Let the hair dry naturally, leave on for at least 8 hours or overnight, then wash out with normal shampoo. Repeat after 7 days (two applications 7 days apart are needed because the effect on eggs is weaker).
items.tag: Head lice (UK 4% lotion; adults and children 6 months and over)

src.q: Apply sufficient lotion to cover dry hair from the base to the tip to ensure that no part of the scalp is left uncovered.
Hedrin should be left on hair for a minimum of 8 hours or overnight.
Wash out with normal shampoo, rinsing thoroughly with water. Repeat the treatment after seven days.
It is less effective in its ovicidal activity and therefore two applications 7 days apart are required.

items.t: Licensed for adults and children aged 6 months and above. Children under 6 months should only be treated under medical supervision.

src.q: Adults and children (aged six months and above)
Children under the age of six months should only be treated under medical supervision.

items.t: Hypersensitivity to any of the ingredients.

src.q: 4.3 Contraindications Hypersensitivity to any of the ingredients

items.t: Stop at the first sign of a skin rash or other hypersensitivity. If signs occur (rash, urticaria, generalised itching, breathing difficulty), shampoo the product off at once and get medical advice if symptoms do not settle.

src.q: Discontinue at the first appearance of a skin rash or any other signs of local or general hypersensitivity.
the product should be shampooed off immediately, and if symptoms do not resolve, medical advice sought

items.t: Fire risk: the lotion is combustible on the hair. Keep treated hair away from open flames, cigarettes and other sources of ignition. MHRA has received reports of serious burns.

src.q: Hedrin 4% cutaneous solution is combustible when on the hair and in direct contact with an open flame or other source of ignition
Eight cases of serious burns associated with Hedrin 4% cutaneous solution have been reported to the MHRA since the product was licensed in 2005.

items.t: For external use only. Avoid contact with the eyes; if it gets into the eyes, flush with water.

src.q: For external use only. Avoid contact with the eyes but if accidentally introduced into the eyes, flush with water.

items.t: One UK SmPC: consult a pharmacist if live lice are found after the second treatment or if head lice keep coming back.

src.q: Consult a pharmacist if live lice are detected after the second treatment or if head lice are a persistent or recurring problem.

items.t: Dimeticone is not known to interact with other medicines; there is little or no absorption through the skin.

src.q: Dimeticone is not known to interact with other drugs
there is little or no absorption of Hedrin through the skin

renal.note: The UK dimeticone 4% SmPCs give no renal advice.

hepatic.note: The UK dimeticone 4% SmPCs give no hepatic advice.

items.t: SmPC: no data suggest it may not be used in pregnancy.

src.q: There is no data to suggest that Hedrin may not be used in pregnancy

items.t: BUMPS: wet combing is the first option in pregnancy. If it fails or is not preferred, physical insecticides such as dimeticone can be used; they do not enter the bloodstream in amounts that could harm the baby.

src.q: Current UK guidelines recommend that pregnant women who need to treat their own or their child's head lice can use 'wet combing'.
If wet combing is not effective or is not preferred, insecticides (products that kill insects) can be used.
Physical insecticides are harmless to humans and also do not enter the bloodstream in amounts that could cause problems for the baby.

items.t: SPS: wet combing or dimeticone are the preferred choices for head lice during breastfeeding. No specific infant monitoring is needed (not absorbed through the skin). Keep hair short or tied up so the infant does not suck treated hair.

src.q: Wet combing or dimeticone are the preferred choices to treat head lice in breastfeeding.
it is not absorbed through the skin, therefore transfer into breast milk is not expected
Keep hair short or tied up to prevent infant from sucking hair during treatment.

reproductive.note: The UK dimeticone 4% SmPCs give no fertility or contraception advice.

items.t: Usually well tolerated. Minor effects: skin irritation, itchy or flaky scalp, irritation around the eyes. Single cases of hair loss reported.

src.q: Dimeticone is usually well tolerated. Minor adverse events include skin irritation, an itchy or flaky scalp and irritation around the eyes.
Single cases of hair loss have been reported.

items.t: Hypersensitivity (rash, urticaria, generalised itching, breathing difficulty): shampoo off at once; seek medical advice if symptoms do not resolve.

src.q: Signs of hypersensitivity reactions including rash, urticaria, generalised pruritus, and breathing difficulties.
the product should be shampooed off immediately, and if symptoms do not resolve, medical advice sought

items.t: Serious burns if treated hair meets a flame or other ignition source (for example lighting a cigarette).

src.q: some products for the eradication of head lice infestations are combustible/flammable when on the hair and can ignite and cause serious harm in the presence of an open flame or other source of ignition such as when lighting cigarettes

items.t: If live lice are still found after the second treatment, or lice keep returning, seek pharmacist advice (one UK SmPC).

src.q: Consult a pharmacist if live lice are detected after the second treatment or if head lice are a persistent or recurring problem.

items.t: External use on the hair and scalp only. Apply to dry hair, work in from roots to tips, let it dry naturally, leave on at least 8 hours or overnight, then wash out with normal shampoo.

src.q: For topical external use only
Work into the hair spreading the liquid evenly from roots to tips. Allow hair to dry naturally.

items.t: Spilt product can make smooth floors slippery.

src.q: Care should be taken as the product may cause a slip hazard if accidentally spilt onto smooth surfaces.

items.t: Do not smoke near treated hair and keep it away from open flames and other ignition sources, including the morning after an overnight application, until the hair is washed.

src.q: they should not smoke around treated hair and that it should be kept away from open flames or other sources of ignition, including in the morning after overnight application until hair is washed

items.t: Treat again after 7 days. Keep the product out of the eyes.

src.q: Repeat the treatment after seven days.
Avoid contact with the eyes
